# telegram-ai-cli

> A CLI and MCP (Model Context Protocol) server, built from one Python codebase,
> that lets an AI agent — Claude, Codex, or any MCP client — read and act on a
> personal Telegram account over MTProto (Telethon), the protocol Telegram's own
> apps use, not the Bot API. Reads (chats, messages, search, whois, members,
> media) run immediately. Anything that changes something on Telegram (send,
> edit, delete, forward, join, leave, invite, promote, mark read, change profile)
> goes through an explicit plan, then a separate apply step, never straight from
> a model's tool call. Chats are gated by an allowlist (private messages closed
> until named explicitly; `777000` and Saved Messages closed unconditionally),
> every outgoing action is written to a two-phase audit log, and rate limits
> persist across process restarts.

## Key facts

- Package/command: `telegram-ai-cli` (PyPI name reserved for a future release;
  not published yet), CLI binary `tg-ai`.
- License: MIT.
- Language: Python, requires 3.12+.
- Protocol library: Telethon (MTProto), not the Telegram Bot API.
- Two surfaces from one codebase: `tg-ai <command>` (CLI) and `tg-ai mcp`
  (stdio MCP server) — same operation registry, same JSON contract.
- Safety model: plan-and-apply for every write; no MCP tool applies a plan.
  For MCP clients that also have shell access (Claude Code, Codex), the
  project states plainly that this boundary is not absolute — see the Safety
  section of the README and `docs/threat-model.md`.
- Status as of 2026-08: pre-alpha, under active development. Not yet published
  to PyPI or an MCP registry (a deliberate, separate decision — a package name
  in a public registry is claimed permanently).

## Primary sources

- [README](https://github.com/stufently/telegram-ai-cli/blob/main/README.md):
  what it does, install and configure, how to add it to Claude Code, Claude
  Desktop, Codex or Cursor, the MCP tool list, the JSON contract, and an FAQ
  written against real questions people ask about Telegram automation and MCP.
- [SECURITY.md](https://github.com/stufently/telegram-ai-cli/blob/main/SECURITY.md):
  vulnerability reporting (GitHub Security Advisories, not email), scope, and
  the design rationale behind each safety control.
- [docs/operations.md](https://github.com/stufently/telegram-ai-cli/blob/main/docs/operations.md):
  every operation on both surfaces — the eight read tools, the twelve plan
  tools, the plan lifecycle commands and the two terminal-only account
  commands — with arguments, defaults and the policy each one consults.
- [docs/configuration.md](https://github.com/stufently/telegram-ai-cli/blob/main/docs/configuration.md):
  the full `tgai.yaml` reference and its `TGAI_`-prefixed environment
  equivalents, including what cannot be configured at all (`777000` and Saved
  Messages are constants in code, not defaults).
- [docs/threat-model.md](https://github.com/stufently/telegram-ai-cli/blob/main/docs/threat-model.md):
  the full threat model, including the honest limit of the plan/apply
  approval boundary and the path to a stronger one (a separate OS principal,
  or a TOTP-gated apply) that v0.1 does not implement.
- [CHANGELOG.md](https://github.com/stufently/telegram-ai-cli/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md):
  what has actually shipped, in Keep a Changelog format.
- [CITATION.cff](https://github.com/stufently/telegram-ai-cli/blob/main/CITATION.cff):
  how to cite this project.

## Related projects, same author (GitHub: stufently)

- [zabbix-ai-cli](https://github.com/stufently/zabbix-ai-cli) — the same
  CLI-plus-MCP-server, plan-and-apply pattern, applied to Zabbix monitoring.
- [yandex-mcp](https://github.com/stufently/yandex-mcp) — MCP servers for
  Yandex Search, Wordstat, Webmaster, Metrika and Direct.

## What this is not

- Not a Telegram Bot API wrapper — it operates a personal user account, which
  has different capabilities (and different risks) than a bot account.
- Not a bulk-messaging or member-scraping tool. Telegram limits and bans
  accounts for that kind of automation regardless of what client sent it.
- Not a `tdata` format converter — `tdata` parsing is delegated to
  `opentele-ng`.
